prior_importants.description: Only a moved events-file mtime stops the next hold, and a hold moves it only when its turn's Stop hook fires. A hold whose turn dies (API error, no Stop) or runs past one sweep is typed again every 15 s, which can spend all eight holds in about two minutes.

A hold is typed into a turn that is already running, because typing a prompt never moves the events file. Three cases: the hold's own turn, a just-recorded steer or peer message, or a resume from the same sweep.

A hold whose turn dies on an API error turns a worker waiting on an open question into a watchdog resume target. The watchdog then types RESUME_MESSAGE ("Continue the task ... run pup session done") while the question is still open.

findings.description: The watchdog decides a dead turn is the hold's only because the newest recorded prompt is a `cache_hold`. A turn started by an unrecorded prompt after the hold (text typed into the attached pane) can still die, and the watchdog then never resumes it, so the session stays STALLED with no `turn_died`. Before this change that turn was resumed.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Line 121 skips the resume whenever the newest prompt event is a hold:

```ts
if (lastPrompt(listEvents(db, sessionId).reverse())?.type === 'cache_hold') return undefined;
```

The comment and ADR 0179 read this as "the turn that died is the hold's". That is only true if every prompt that reaches the pane is recorded. Text typed by hand into the window is never recorded, and typing by hand is a documented operator path:
- The watchdog's own header describes the operator typing into the window.
- ADR 0007 L29-37 says unblock "steers nothing … The operator has already typed what they wanted typed".
- `pup unblock` (`src/cli/ui/actions.service.ts` L189-190) records no prompt.

**Triggers.**
1. A `running` worker with an open question is held, and the hold's turn ends normally. The operator answers by typing into the pane through `pup attach` rather than `pup answer`. That working turn later dies on `API Error: Connection lost…`.
2. An `awaiting-review` session is held. The gate then blocks it at the reject cap: `rejectOrBlock` returns before the `steer` append (`merge-gate.service.ts` L3613-3618). The operator types the fix into the pane and runs `pup unblock`. A turn that dies after that is never resumed.

In both cases `findStalledSessions` lists the session on every sweep. `resumeSession` returns `undefined` before it reads the pane, so no `turn_died` is written and nothing is typed. Before this delta the dead turn was resumed. This is the stranded-overnight case the watchdog exists to prevent. The new test in `turn-watchdog.test.ts` covers only a hold with no later file move.

**Fix.** `stalledAt` is the events file's mtime. A hold's own dead turn fires no hook, so the file has not moved since the hold. A hold whose turn ended has a Stop after it. So skip only a hold recorded at or after the file's last move, compared at whole seconds the same way `holdDue` does. One edge stays open: a hold turn that reaches a tool before it dies would be resumed. `CACHE_HOLD_MESSAGE` tells the worker to run no tool, which keeps that edge narrow.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ea1570c72f9fef7abb629f5200185689a11a6cc0/src/core/turn-watchdog.service.ts#L118-L121
